meta.name: Great American Design System
meta.note: This file is the only place a value is typed. Everything in build/ is generated. Prose rules live in DESIGN-SYSTEM.md and must never restate a value from here.

navy-lt.use: Secondary structure, quiet hairline on dark panels

navy-pale.use: Quiet text on dark grounds, dividers that must read on navy

ink.use: Dark ground. Footer, scrims, caption bars. Not a text color

mortar.use: Panel and column fill, text on navy

tabby.use: Primary text on dark grounds, hairline rung on light grounds

aggregate.use: Group divider, section break, table outer edge, coquina texture

persimmon-lt.use: Small text on navy, accent rules on navy

persimmon.use: Mid accent, large text on light grounds

aqua-lt.use: Light step 2, dark step 1. The only aqua that carries text

navy.note: Logo update to this value in progress. Any spec established against #1F4E79 is void.

cherry.note: Confirmed from the color chart. Inside coated CMYK gamut, no spot ink required.

stack.sans: "Nunito Sans Variable", "Nunito Sans", ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif

docx._note: One family per weight. Word resolves a family name literally and cannot address a variable weight axis, so every weight and slant is its own family here. Never set bold or italic flags on these in a document build — see assets.fonts.note. "body" and "utility" are the pre-1.2.0 names for body400 and utility400, kept so consumers pinned to 1.1.x do not break; prefer the weighted keys.

font.note: Variable family names come first so self-hosted @fontsource-variable resolves; the static name is the fallback for consumers loading from Google. Whichever is loaded wins, the other is inert. docx keeps the static names only — Word resolves the family literally. Never set bold:true on an Archivo run in docx; weight lives in the family name.

typeMap.flag: Spec table says 12px; prose below it says 10pt (13.3px). Unresolved.

motif.note: Tiles run dark to light, left to right, never reversed, at all three scales. The 14px glyph never stands alone.

gradient._note: Built from colour tokens so no consumer retypes an aqua value. The band separator uses var(--ground) so it follows the surface: sand on web, paper on a document page root. Band geometry verified against the site 2026-07-30: it is a repeating tile at the fixed tile.divider scale, period 3 tiles + 3 gaps, with a trailing separator after the last tile. The cap is different on purpose — it stretches to the card width, so it stays on percentage thirds.

page.note: US Letter, half inch margins. The margin is half an inch because a 36-row reference table does not fit at one inch.

retired.reason: orphan red, 11.6 dE from the logo
old navy-600, persimmon-lt fails on it
NOT retired. This is cherry. Listed only to prevent reintroduction as persimmon-dk
old persimmon-lt, fails AA at sizes in use

documents._note: Document type registry. Each entry says what an artifact IS, so a request like 'make me a price sheet' resolves to structure and type roles rather than a generic table. Ground and motifs are properties of the artifact, decided at design time. Printing never transforms them.

price-sheet.structure: Cover masthead, effective date, column header row, grouped part rows with group labels, footnotes. Continuation pages use the continuation masthead.

warranty.structure: Cover masthead, numbered sections with subsection labels, prose body, exclusions list, claims procedure. Revision number is required and appears in the footer.

return-policy.structure: Cover masthead, numbered sections, prose body, fee table if applicable. Dealer and distributor variants are separate documents, never combined.

rma-form.structure: Cover masthead, instruction block, labelled fill fields with rules beneath, authorization block. Fields must remain writable in print; never place a field over a filled panel.

quote.structure: Cover masthead, customer block, quote number and validity date, line-item table, totals block, terms footnote.

spec-sheet.structure: Cover masthead, product identity block, segment diagram if the product has a part-number structure, dimension and specification tables, key options, footnotes.

agreement.structure: Cover masthead, recitals, numbered clauses with subsection labels, signature block on the final page. Signature lines are rules on paper ground, never on a panel.

flyer.structure: Hero image or product shot, display headline, short benefit copy, one call to action, contact block. Sunburst permitted once, in the hero only.

line-sheet.structure: Cover masthead, product grid with image, name, part number and short spec per cell. Waterline card cap permitted on cells. If prices appear, treat the row budget as binding.

brochure.structure: Cover, narrative spreads alternating image and copy, product summary pages, contact block. Section dividers may use the 26px waterline band.

catalog-cover.structure: Full-bleed image or flat colour field, wordmark, catalog title, edition or year. Sunburst permitted once. No body copy.

radius._note: 2xl was dropped in v1.1.0. It duplicated xl at 20px. Consumers must convert rounded-2xl to rounded-xl; leaving it undefined lets Tailwind's 16px default apply silently.

shadow._note: Warm, hard, directional. Light from the upper left. rgba(92,74,54,*) is the warm shadow base and is deliberate — never a neutral grey. card, photo and menu were back-compat aliases duplicating sm, lg and lg; they do not enter the package.

icon._note: PROVISIONAL. Confirm against real artwork before treating as measured. UI iconography only — this is the drawing system for interface icons, NOT assets.icon, which is the made-in-USA flag identity mark.

assets._note: Brand artefacts. SVG is canonical; raster and print derive from it. Every SVG under assets/ is validated against its treatment's allowed colours, resolved from the filename suffix. clearSpace and minSize stay null until measured against real artwork — conventional numbers are not a substitute for measuring. Source SVGs are tight-cropped to the mark: no padding in the viewBox. All padding comes from the generator, because padding baked into a source compounds with generated padding invisibly — the file looks correct in isolation and wrong everywhere it is used. `npm run build` reports each source's viewBox and aspect ratio so a padded source shows up in the log.

sand.use: Reversed, light on dark, full-colour contexts

icon:full.use: Icon full colour: navy stripes, sand stars. Kind-scoped — overrides the shared `full` for assets.icon only, because the icon's full colour is not the logo's. Scoped keys carry a colon, which no filename suffix can contain, so they are never resolved from a filename.

clearSpace._note: Measured against real artwork. `unit` names the reference measure (e.g. 'cap-height of the wordmark', 'width of the mark'); `multiple` is how many of that unit must stay clear on all sides. Conventional values are not a substitute for measuring.

logo.pending: Wordmark, mark and print masters. The primary lockup landed in revision 1.1.0 with the navy recolour from #1F4E79 to #1F3A5F complete — #1F4E79 is retired and the SVG check rejects it, so nothing can regress to it silently. assets/logo/wordmark/ and assets/logo/mark/ are still empty, and print EPS/PDF come from the artwork producer as CMYK or spot, outside this repo's validation.

icon.note: Stylized flag in brand colours, not a literal US flag. Two-tone: navy stripes with sand stars, because the stars have to stand against the flag rather than disappear into it. Its full colour is therefore navy + sand, not the logo's navy + cherry, which is why assets.treatments carries a kind-scoped "icon:full". The sand, white and black treatments are single colour and drop the stars entirely rather than render them in the flag's own colour, where they would not read — 25 paths in the full-colour file, 6 in each of the others. Still four treatments. A literal flag would carry Old Glory Red #B31942 and Old Glory Blue #0A3161, neither in the palette, and would need a documented exemption; this needs none, since navy and sand are both palette colours. Usually sits beside a made-in-USA claim, so it forms part of that claim.

clearSpace._note: Measured against real artwork. `unit` names the reference measure (e.g. 'cap-height of the wordmark', 'width of the mark'); `multiple` is how many of that unit must stay clear on all sides. Conventional values are not a substitute for measuring.

fonts.note: Statics are committed because nothing can fetch them: Google ships Archivo, Oswald and Nunito Sans as variable fonts. Satisfy is already static. Archivo's variable default instance is SemiBold and Nunito Sans's default weight is 200; unpinned instances render wrong with no error. Every weight is its own family — never set bold or italic flags in docx.

raster._note: Generated by `npm run raster` from the SVG sources. Never hand-edit; edits are silently overwritten on the next run. Output lives under assets/raster/, separate from the source directories, so nothing generated sits beside artwork where it could be mistaken for a source and edited. It is committed to the repo deliberately: it means anyone can take a PNG straight from a GitHub URL without cloning, installing or building anything, which is the path for everyone here who is not a developer. Regenerate and commit the PNGs in the SAME commit as the SVG change — a source and its raster drifting apart is the failure this exists to prevent. `pad` is a fraction of the longest rendered edge, added on all four sides as transparent pixels; declared sizes are FINAL dimensions including it. Padding is not clear space — clear space is a placement rule in any medium, this is pixels baked into a file that cannot enforce one, and the two are separate numbers on purpose. Favicons use 0 deliberately: they are meant to read edge-to-edge, and at 16px even 12% padding costs roughly a fifth of the mark. The 0.06 on logos is a starting value, not a measured one — once assets.logo.clearSpace is filled in from real artwork, revisit whether generated padding should match it.
